name: Lenacapavir
route_note: subcutaneous injection every 6 months, after an oral tablet loading phase

discovery.note: Developed from Gilead's capsid-targeting programme; extremely high potency and low solubility allow a twice-yearly depot. Year of the first published description (GS-6207; Link et al., Nature 2020).

tagline: First HIV capsid inhibitor; two injections a year prevent HIV almost completely
summary: Lenacapavir is the first HIV-1 capsid inhibitor, potent enough to be given as a subcutaneous injection only twice a year. It was first approved for multidrug-resistant HIV and in 2025 for pre-exposure prophylaxis, after trials in which it prevented nearly all infections. Science named it the 2024 Breakthrough of the Year.
mechanism: The HIV capsid is a cone-shaped shell of p24 protein that protects the viral genome, guides it to the nucleus and then comes apart in a controlled way. Lenacapavir binds the interface between adjacent capsid subunits, where host factors such as CPSF6 and Nup153 also bind.

By hyper-stabilising and distorting the capsid, it disrupts nuclear import of viral DNA, virus assembly and formation of a normal capsid in new particles, so it acts at several stages of the life cycle. Resistance mutations such as M66I and Q67H reduce susceptibility; there is no cross-resistance with other drug classes.
uses: Multidrug-resistant HIV-1 infection in heavily treatment-experienced adults, with an optimised background regimen (Sunlenca)
HIV-1 pre-exposure prophylaxis in adults and adolescents weighing at least 35 kg (Yeztugo/Yeytuo)

history.title: First clinical data
history.detail: Gilead describes GS-6207 and its sustained antiviral activity after a single injection (Nature 2020).

history.title: First approval
history.detail: The EU approves Sunlenca in August 2022 and the FDA in December 2022 for multidrug-resistant HIV.

history.title: PURPOSE 1
history.detail: The PrEP trial in young women in South Africa and Uganda reports zero HIV infections among those receiving lenacapavir; PURPOSE 2 in men and gender-diverse people also shows very high efficacy.

history.title: Generic licences
history.detail: Gilead signs royalty-free voluntary licences with six generic manufacturers to supply 120 low- and middle-income countries; Science names lenacapavir its Breakthrough of the Year.

history.title: PrEP approval
history.detail: The FDA approves Yeztugo for PrEP in June 2025; WHO recommends lenacapavir PrEP in July, and the EU approves it in August.

pk.half_life: oral about 10–12 days; subcutaneous apparent half-life about 8–12 weeks
pk.metabolism: CYP3A, UGT1A1 and P-glycoprotein substrate; moderate CYP3A inhibitor

serious: emergence of resistance if HIV is acquired while drug levels decline
safety.boxed_warning: Yeztugo: risk of drug resistance if used for PrEP in undiagnosed HIV-1 infection (US label).

facts: Lenacapavir's twice-yearly dosing is the longest dosing interval of any approved HIV medicine.
Injected drug forms a depot under the skin from which it is released slowly over months.
Drug levels can persist for a year or more after the last injection.

references.title: Bekker LG et al. Twice-yearly lenacapavir or daily F/TAF for HIV prevention in cisgender women (PURPOSE 1). NEJM 2024
Gilead: European Commission authorizes Yeytuo for HIV prevention (August 2025)
